claim: Since February 1, 2024 AWS charges $0.005 per IP per hour for public IPv4 addresses, whether in use or idle, including the public IPv4 addresses of running instances and Elastic IP addresses; before that date an in-use public IPv4 address had no charge. Addresses in an Amazon-provided contiguous IPv4 block have their own hourly rate.

qualifiers.scope: per public IPv4 address, per hour
qualifiers.condition: the Amazon-provided contiguous IPv4 block has a separate hourly rate

evidence.quote: Effective February 1, 2024 there will be a charge of $0.005 per IP per hour for all public IPv4 addresses, whether attached to a service or not (there is already a charge for public IPv4 addresses you allocate in your account but don’t attach to an EC2 instance).

| In-use Public IPv4 address (including Amazon provided public IPv4 and Elastic IP) assigned to resources in your VPC, Amazon Global Accelerator, and AWS Site-to-site VPN tunnel | No charge | $0.005 |
evidence.table_header: | Public IP Address Type | Current Price/Hour (USD) | New Price/Hour (USD) (Effective February 1, 2024) |

evidence.quote: AWS charges for all public IPv4 addresses, including public IPv4 addresses associated with running instances and Elastic IP addresses.

The price is the same whether the public IPv4 address is in-use public IPv4 addresses that is associated with an AWS resource you own, or an idle public IPv4 addresses in your AWS account not associated with any AWS resources.
You pay an hourly rate for each public IPv4 address in the Amazon-provided contiguous IPv4 block.
